questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: An English-speaking location, good electives, a unique culture, and a lot to explore.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy - the host university gives most of the necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got assistance with changing my subjects as I had some time schedule issues.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in Queen Mary Building with a lot of other exchange students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were shared kitchen facilities at my housing. It was surprisingly rarely crowded and worked better than expected.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Living on campus makes it easy to meet other exchange students and socialize.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't get my courses until about a month before my arrival, and many of my preferred choices weren't available. So I had to apply for additional courses once I got to Australia, which was a bit stressful — but it all worked out in the end.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Some courses were pre-approved, but for most of them you had to apply so they could determine whether you had the necessary skills/knowledge to take the course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write to your counsellor, but getting a reply could take some time. There was also a student help desk located on campus.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Most of my preferred classes weren't available, but they were very helpful in registering me for alternative courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for plenty of classes so you can build a timetable that fits together. Be prepared that you might not get your preferred classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was similar to at home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was very different, as some of my classes included grades for participation. You were therefore expected to take part in class, and attendance was required.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Media Law: Contempt and Open Justice, War Law: Use of Force and Humanitarian Law, Philosophy of Criminal Law and United Nations, Peace and Security.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend War Law. The teacher used a lot of real-life examples, and the structure of the class made it more interesting. I would also recommend Philosophy of Criminal Law if you are looking for a class that is not too reading-heavy.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Overseas Healthcare Cover

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries and rent were more expensive than expected. However, eating out was cheaper compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The University has multiple clubs and sports available. Personally, I joined the Muay Thai club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surfing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Other places in Australia — personally, I did a road trip along the east coast with some other exchange students, which was great. You could also go to the Blue Mountains for a short trip.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy — very similar to Denmark, although people are much more open to talking to strangers.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Approach people in your classes and join different clubs. Go to the university-hosted events at the start of the year.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There wasn't anything too challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They were very laid back and welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: "1) Go to the orientation events to get to know other students — I met a lot of people who I spent the rest of the semester with. 2) There are a lot of exchange students, so it's easy to make friends. 3) Time goes by faster than you think, so make sure to do all the things you want to while you're there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All of the different places I visited and the new friends I made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Participating in classes. It can be challenging at the start, especially when you're in a new environment. But they're used to exchange students, and both the classmates and teachers were very supportive.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
